strengths: Demonstrates practical value of cascaded pretrained models achieving competitive performance without dataset-specific fine-tuning, addressing a real problem in TQA deployment
Strong robustness under query paraphrasing (Table 2): CRAFT maintains 0.04 point drop vs. DTR's 8.38+ point degradation, suggesting better generalization
Comprehensive stage-wise ablations showing clear incremental gains and transparent methodology
Well-written with clear figures and attention to practical deployment considerations (token consumption analysis showing 70% reduction)

Practical insights on computational efficiency showing 70%+ token reduction with sub-table representations
Clear, modular pipeline design with well-articulated progression from efficient sparse to expensive dense retrievers
Evaluation across multiple LLMs (Mistral, Llama3, Qwen) and few-shot configurations with extensive end-to-end results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: purely combines existing models (SPLADE 2021, Sentence Transformers, text-embedding-3-small, Gemini Flash) with no new methods; contribution is orchestration and threshold selection rather than methodological innovation

Misleading 'training-free' framing: heavily depends on proprietary pretrained models (Gemini 1.5 Flash, OpenAI embeddings, SPLADE) trained on vast data; only avoids TQA-specific training, not training altogether

Unfair baseline comparison: CRAFT benefits from Gemini-generated table descriptions and query decompositions that baselines lack; critical ablation showing isolated contribution of this preprocessing relative to cascaded retrieval is missing

Severely limited reproducibility: depends critically on proprietary commercial APIs (Gemini Flash, text-embedding-3-small) for both preprocessing and embedding; no code release mentioned; generating 169K table descriptions incurs unmeasured latency and cost
Evaluation limited to single dataset (NQ-Tables only) with no cross-dataset validation; significantly limits generalizability claims; standard for NLP would require 2-3 datasets

R@1 performance substantially worse than THYME (41.13 vs 48.55, a 7.4 point gap); explanation dismissed as inevitable but not investigated; suggests the cascade may sacrifice top-1 accuracy despite overall gains

Missing computational cost analysis: 3-stage pipeline latency overhead unquantified; API call costs for 169K tables not reported; trade-off between accuracy and practical deployment costs not rigorously addressed

strengths: Clear practical motivation addressing adaptability and training-free approaches for TQA
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with thorough ablations, robustness testing, and multi-LLM end-to-end analysis
Strong empirical results, particularly competitive R@10/R@50 metrics and impressive robustness to query paraphrasing
Well-written with clear presentation, detailed methodology, and practical efficiency analysis (token consumption)
Insightful robustness study comparing CRAFT to fine-tuned methods under query perturbation

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablation studies, robustness testing via query paraphrasing, and end-to-end evaluation across multiple LLMs

Mini-table design effectively reduces noise in downstream QA; convincing case studies (Tables 16-17) demonstrate benefits even when gold tables are retrieved at moderate ranks
Thorough robustness analysis showing near-perfect recovery under query paraphrasing (0.04% drop vs. 6-12% for DTR), demonstrating superior generalization vs. fine-tuned methods
Detailed error analysis with qualitative case studies providing insights into failure modes and when intermediate representations improve reasoning
Reproducibility: clear implementation details, prompts in appendix, code promised, transparent hyperparameter reporting
weaknesses: Misleading 'training-free' framing: all components use pre-trained models from massive datasets (Gemini, OpenAI text-embedding-3, Sentence Transformer); more accurately 'dataset-specific fine-tuning free' rather than truly training-free

Overstated claims on OTT-QA: paper emphasizes 'competitive results' at higher recalls, but R@1 gap vs. THYME is substantial (55.56 vs. 66.67, 11.1 points); end-to-end evaluation uses oracle setup with gold passages (not true open-retrieval), significantly weakening claims

Unfair comparison concerns: text-embedding-3-large (Stage 3) is a recent proprietary model newer than most baselines; unclear whether NQ-Tables SOTA improvement comes from the method vs. superior embeddings; missing ablation using earlier embedding models

Insufficient design justification: why different models for Stage 2 vs. Stage 3? How sensitive to mini-table row count (5 rows)? Limited exploration of alternative cascade configurations; preprocessing row ranking via Sentence Transformer adds non-trivial computation

Robustness evaluation limited to single paraphrasing approach and DTR baseline; few-shot results (Table 14) show high variance without statistical significance testing; no multiple runs or error bars; only single-hop and oracle multi-hop evaluation

strengths: Strong empirical results on NQ-Tables (R@1 = 49.84%) with comprehensive evaluation across multiple metrics and datasets

Detailed error analysis and case studies (Appendix D) providing valuable qualitative insights into failure modes and design benefits
Practical modular design allowing component swapping and seamless integration of new embedding models
weaknesses: Limited novelty: cascaded retrieval is well-established (Wang et al. 2011; Hu et al. 2019); primary contribution is engineering with existing models rather than methodological advance
